thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for streaming API in us-east-1 (service: streaming.v1). p95=320ms p99=2.1s over last 5m. Error spike and increased TLS handshake times observed. Paging oncall: @sre-oncall @net-oncall :rotating_light:

sam: saw that, grabbing logs. Any customer-impact flags yet?

maria: CS flagged 3 customers with streaming stalls, one reporting reconnections ~every 15s. Ticket 9876 opened.

taylor: adding context from dashboards — tail latency spike aligns with cross-AZ NAT egress error rate increase starting 15:23 UTC. Traces show TLS handshake latency jumps to 800-1200ms at p99.

net-oncall: investigating VPC egress path. I see increased retransmits between AZ-b and nat-egress-b. Running quick checks:
```
# from a control plane host
> sudo tcptrace -i eth0 | grep retrans
> sudo ip route get 8.8.8.8
> curl -sS -D - https://streaming.internal/health | head -n 20
```
Outputs: packet loss spikes ~3-6% on nic-to-gw, route shows primary NAT gateway in AZ-b, long handshake times observed.

sre-oncall: can we fail traffic to an alternate NAT/gateway or route through nat-a? If cross-zone path is flaky that explains p99 tail.

net-oncall: can do a weighted routing change in the VPC egress route table; preparing a quick rollback plan. Will shift 30% traffic to nat-a for the next 10m, monitor p99.

ops-lead: thumbs up. Coordinate on-call handoff if this stretches past our shift. Also notify infra to stand by for NAT replacement if needed.

maria: CS ping: put a short message in affected customers that we’re investigating latency and may see reconnections; ETA 15m for mitigation. /cc @customer-success-bot

customer-success-bot: Draft msg: "We're investigating streaming disruptions in us-east-1 (affecting streaming.v1). Engineers are actively mitigating; we'll update within 15 minutes." Approve? :white_check_mark:

sam: implementing routing shift now. Command: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0a111
# then adjust weights on gateway-level LB
```
Switch started at 15:32:10 UTC.

incident-bot: ACTION: applied partial egress weight shift (30% -> nat-a) at 15:32:27 UTC. Monitoring p95/p99 for 10m window.

maria: CS updated customers at 15:33 UTC.

net-oncall: after shift, retransmits down from 5% -> 0.5% on the shifted traffic path. TLS handshake p99 reduced to ~450ms on nat-a path. Aggregate p99 dropped to 1.0s from 2.1s.

taylor: still seeing some streaming stalls — looks like cached connections pinned to old NAT for certain long-lived streams, causing tail stalls during handshake fallback. Need to force reconnects for affected streams or route NAT stateful flows.

sre-oncall: can we push a rolling kill to affected edge nodes to force clients to re-establish with new egress path? Doing that will cause short disconnects but reduce tail.

ops-lead: coordinate with CS before aggressive kill. Maria?

maria: approved — tell me expected customer-visible blip. We should give a heads-up 30s prior to action.

sam: preparing a targeted restart script for edge pods in us-east-1 with label streaming-edge=hot; will restart 10% at a time, 30s pause.

net-oncall: also found TLS handshake log samples showing repeated ClientHello retransmits. Suspect NAT device CPU bursts + packet drops during transient GC. Filed infra ticket to swap NAT instance: INFRA-4521.

sre-oncall: start rolling restarts at 15:41 UTC. Script snippet: 
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/streaming-edge -n prod --selector=streaming-edge=hot --max-unavailable=1
# loop with sleep 30
```
Restart sequence started.

incident-bot: NOTE: maintenance window - rolling restarts in progress (15:41 - ongoing). Monitor streaming p99.

maria: informing customers: "We're restarting a subset of edge nodes to stabilise streaming connections. You may see brief reconnects (seconds) while we complete mitigation."

customer-success-bot: Posted to affected customers channel.

net-oncall: NAT instance swap initiated in parallel (INFRA-4521). If NAT swap completes, we expect handshake stability for existing connections.

sam: after two waves of restarts and routing shift, p99 is down to 420ms, p95 ~170ms. Error rates trending down. Still monitoring for residual stalls.

maria: CS reporting reduced tickets; one Enterprise customer still saw two reconnects but accepts mitigation summary.

ops-lead: good. Prepare for on-call handoff in 45m. Document actions taken and open follow-ups.

sre-oncall: opening follow-ups: 
- NET-254: run packet capture correlation for nat-b during 15:20-15:40 UTC (pcap stored)
- INFRA-4521: NAT instance CPU/firmware analysis + swap logs
- RUNTIME-773: improve connection affinity fallback to avoid stale NAT pinning
- POSTMORTEM-1793005123: full incident writeup and customer-impact summary

net-oncall: adding network-side recommended immediate ops: add health-check amplification for NAT to detect CPU GC earlier, and add a transient 5s flow-evict policy when we detect >1% retransmit across AZ.

taylor: I’ll create a regression alert for streaming p99/TLS-handshake that ties to model routing and cross-zone NAT metrics so we get faster automated failover.

sam: swapping NAT completed at 15:55 UTC per infra. Observed handshake p99 fall to ~180ms after swap for flows that reconnected.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: aggregated p99 back within SLO (p99<250ms) at 15:59 UTC. Incident state: mitigated. Postmortem scheduled.

maria: CS: sending incident update to impacted customers with summary + ETA for postmortem (EOD).

ops-lead: preparing handoff notes for next oncall: include timeline, mitigations, and follow-ups.

sre-oncall: handoff to morning oncall @sre-oncall-next at 16:30 UTC, will maintain monitoring for 2h.

sam: final checks — logs and tracing show residual short-lived stalls only for older client connections that never reconnected; will include remediation steps in postmortem to force aggressive affinity reset on rollover.

maria: thanks team. Kudos for quick partial routing + NAT swap plan that minimized customer impact. :clap:

incident-bot: Created POSTMORTEM-1793005123 and assigned to oncall/sre. Tags: network, nat, tls-handshake, streaming, cross-az.

ops-lead: closing thread for now. Please add any additional notes to the postmortem doc.
